Sentence (English): It was between an LG and Bosch dishwasher when our old one reached end of life.
Comments (English): [ I Expected Nothing Less From a Bosch Product ] || ---------------- || It was between an LG and Bosch dishwasher when our old one reached end of life. The 500 series is full-featured enough for the daily needs of two people and the occasional heavy lifting when a crowd shows up (Thanksgiving, Christmas, etc.). Installation went smoothly through the retailer's service. At first the filter well filled up with water and the dishes were wet upon completion of a cycle, but a call to a support engineer (who was all business) solved that problem. As it turned out, the hose to the air gap needed some cleaning. Things went smoothly after that. Another call to support concerned the remote control of the unit through the Home Connect application on my iPhone. While there is still local control of the dishwasher on the door panel, Bosch is clearly moving towards the use of the app since, more features are available there then on the unit itself, several of which I activated. I will be calling support this coming week regarding restarting the WiFi should it become disconnected. It's not immediately apparent how that works, nor does it appear to be a straightforward procedure. Aside from that, the fit and finish of the machine are very good and the third rack, near the top of the interior is an excellent feature when you have filled up the silverware tray (a bit small). So far, so good!

We want to use the machine to wash four people's dishes from two days, not just dishes from one fancy dinner, and the design doesn't allow enough flexibility Our serving dishes don't fit around the outside, for example, where the loading instructions suggest that we put them, and if we try to put serving dishes anywhere else then there won't be room for all of them or for many of our miscellaneous smaller dishes. Also the dishes that we use for salad bowls are too deep to fit anywhere on the bottom rack, and when arranged on the top rack they fall over with a clatter whenever the rack is pushed in or pulled out. And the hose thing that attaches to the faucet does not want to go all the way back into the machine between uses.

Sentence (English): We had an lg that broke after 6 years and this bosch 800 is taking its place.
Comments (English): [ Is Bosch 800 Worth It? ] || ---------------- || We had an lg that broke after 6 years and this bosch 800 is taking its place. We have had it for almost a month. The bosch is a little quieter than our old lg. The bosch racking set up is way worse than our old lg and we cannot get as many dishes in. We use a lot of tupperware and reusable plastic. The bosch 800 is said to be able to dry all the plastic and lids. The dishes dont get any dryer than our old lg and that is with using the special crystal dry cylce that takes 2.5 hours. We still need to air dry the plastics. We also cannot get the speed 60 wash to work. It keeps coming up as 80 min instead of 60. We bought this for the speed 60 and the ability to dry all of the plastics and lids and the bosch 800 doesnt do this for us. The app does nothing to answer any questions. I will be calling bosch directly after the holidays but in the mean time, it is not better than our old lg. Hopefully we can figure it out so we can justify the almost double the price tag.

Sentence (English): Our 8 year old Kitchenaid started to leak badly and our handyman recommended that we get a new dishwasher rather than getting it fixed.
Comments (English): [ I Really Like Our New Bosch Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Our 8 year old Kitchenaid started to leak badly and our handyman recommended that we get a new dishwasher rather than getting it fixed. I had been told by many of my friends that Bosch was a great brand. I went to the largest appliance store in the Chicago Suburbs and asked to see Bosch Dishwashers. The salesperson took a lot of time explaining how Bosh works differently than most dishwashers, demonstrating all the features of each Series. He even showed me how to clean the filter! He also said almost anything I would want to know about Bosch dishwashers are also on line (which I found to be true). I ordered an 800 Series and chose one that would look good with my other appliances. It was delivered soon and installed. I think I made the right choice. This dishwasher makes no sounds, cleans great, even on a 1 hour cycle. The only slight negative is that some tops of cups and plastics need to be blotted with a towel to get the wet off (sort of like my old Kitchenaid). But even so, I would recommend it.

Sentence (English): I thought I had purchased a high-performance product after my ultra-decade-old electrolux.
Comments (English): [ All smoke no roast ] || ---------------- || I thought I had purchased a high-performance product after my ultra-decade-old electrolux. Instead, it's a piece of cake. Lots of technology and little substance. The dishes are not cleaned (I use liquid pril) even with the longest washes. The old dishwasher with the quick wash returned clean plates and glasses. Then the upper basket for cutlery takes up a lot of space and compromises the washing possibilities of the tallest pots. I therefore do not recommend purchasing it.
Comments (Original): [ Tutto fumo niente arrosto ] || ---------------- || Credevo di aver acquistato un prodotto performante dopo la mia ultradecennale electrolux. Invece un piffero. La Vecchia lavastoviglie con il lavaggio rapido restituiva piatti e bicchieri lindi. Poi il cestello superiore per le posate toglie tanto spazio e pregiudica le possibilità di lavaggio delle pentole più alte. Non consiglio quindi l'acquisto.

Sentence (English): We had to replace a Technica (Bellissimo) that for the 2 time had rusting baskets and more recently a busted dispenser due to dropping a plate on it.
Comments (English): [ Best choice for the $$$ ] || ---------------- || We had to replace a Technica (Bellissimo) that for the 2 time had rusting baskets and more recently a busted dispenser due to dropping a plate on it. So we weren't looking to spend a whole lot of money considering even some of the best brands/models had reviews that expressed all kinds of issues and poor backup service. The Haier however, had pretty good reviews (or at least reviews where we were willing to accept the negatives) and the price was what we were willing to pay for such an appliance. The online ordering, payment and delivery were great. The dishwasher itself was as easy to install as any. I was actually surprised to see a few simple little quality of life features I didn't expect from a cheaper priced product like plastic clips on the rear to hold cables/hoses should you need. But other more up-market features like the self opening door after the cycle has finished which is generally only seen on more expensive machines.This machine in it's freestanding form with the top left on was about 50mm taller than our old machine which made for a better fit in the space our builders provided. This made for a more aesthetically pleasing appearance in our kitchen, no more unsightly large gaps. The operation of the machine itself is intuitive in my opinion, logical I would say. Simply put there are 2 rows of options. The top row contains the program selections and the second row contains extended or truncated features to be applied to the program you choose. You adjust each row by pressing the relative >> buttons which progress the selection from left to right. So, press the power button, select your desired program/extras and press start/play. The machine starts and shows a countdown timer (which seemed to be a huge gripe of many people when reviewing other machines that don't have this feature) and away you go. During its operation the machine is very quiet, we can easily have it running while going about our normal routine. In fact, our plan from now on is to put it on before bedtime so that the plastics have a better chance of drying. Depending on the program there does however seem to be times early on where the volume increases during what sounds like high pressure water blasting. I haven't read about every feature of the machine, but I assume it's to loosen stubborn food particles. It doesn't last long, and it doesn't happen throughout the entire cycle. Unfortunately, this won't be a complete review for many people because we like to rinse and remove loose food from our dishes before we "sanitise" them in the dishwasher. We do this to avoid having that old dishwasher cooked food smell in kitchen/living area and we never really have to clean the machine itself. So as far as heavy-duty cycles on dishes and pots that are just scraped and placed in the machine, I can't comment. We typically use the 70 min cycle which is the 60-minute cycle plus the extra drying feature and if we do the overnight wash the only water left on the dishes is what gets trapped in lips/areas that can't be faced down to drain properly. Even then it's not much. I regards to longevity I have no idea since we've only had the machine for about a month as of this review. I will update it should we come across any major issues.

Comments (English): [ If you hesitate, it's a waste of time. ] || ---------------- || Hello, this is Office Mom. When I get home from work, I have to take care of the kids' leftover dishes and clean up after my husband. But lately, the dishwashing that follows has become just too much of a hassle. A coworker raved about dishwashers and strongly recommended that I buy one. Last year, when I replaced our old kitchen sink, I considered getting a built-in model. However, I gave up on the idea because I figured doing it all at once would be too much work. But the moment I realized how difficult it is, I started craving a dishwasher! A 12-place setting model would be nice, but that would be too much of a hassle. It might be a bit small for a family of four—a 4th grader, a 1st year middle schooler, and two adults—but I decided to give it a try anyway. After comparing various models, the Samsung 6-place setting caught my eye! After ordering, they mentioned that a hole needed to be drilled. I told them that the hole for my water purifier was a bit large, and when they came to install it, they routed the line through that hole. The installation took a little over 10 minutes, and I listened to about 5 minutes of instructions. When I first started using it after installation, I thought, "Huh? There are some dishes that aren't cleaned?" and thought I'd messed it up. It turned out that I'm just not very good at Tetris-styled things at an angle. Even if you just throw the dishes in upside down and stack them on top with a little space in between to fill it up completely, it works so, so well! I ran the sticky dishes from bossam on the high setting, and oh my god, where did all that grease go? Even the curry left a trace! It feels a bit small for a 6-person dishwasher with a 4-person capacity, but I am extremely satisfied because it cleans everything perfectly, including a pot for a regular meal. A 12-person capacity would probably be the best, but for a family of four, it cleans a pot for a meal in one go. If you roll them in a zigzag pattern, leaving a gap in the middle, they come out clean even when packed full! I really highly recommend it. >> As for detergent, I use Tamsa 6-person All-in-One, so it is affordable and fits perfectly without having to cut it! I recommend this detergent too. If my review was helpful, please click "Helpful." January 5th. I am still extremely satisfied! When I get home from work in the evening and have a drink with my husband, I usually just fall asleep without doing the dishes because it's such a hassle! It used to be my routine to do the piled-up dishes before leaving for work in the morning, but these days, even if I have a drink, I just rinse them roughly with water, run the dishwasher, and go to sleep, and by morning, 80% of the dishes are dry! I really, really love it. My husband bought it for me, and he teases me, saying I like it more than anything he's bought me before. March 12th. There are still places where it doesn't quite work out perfectly because I'm not good at Tetris sometimes, but that's my problem! Don't hesitate, buy it twice, buy it three times!

Sentence (English): I have been satisfied with the purchase of this dishwasher brand and model.
Comments (English): [ Worth the money ] || ---------------- || I have been satisfied with the purchase of this dishwasher brand and model. The main issue I have that is on the negative side is; the amount of time it takes just to do a load of dishes. The fastest time is an hour and that also means you can't select a dry cycle so the dishes, mainly anything plastic will be very wet when complete. If you add any of the 2 dry cycle options, then you are looking at an additional 45 minutes plus. And if you choose the longest cycle plus steam, it will take over 4 hours for a single load. That definitely makes me wonder how appliances like these are called "energy efficient". Even using Cascade pods and a liquid drying agent, I still have water spots too. But it is what it is, so I'm not over the moon happy but it does do a good job overall. I forgot to mention, the adjustable height for the top rack does come in handy.

Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher - sketchy installation ] || ---------------- || Extremely quiet during dish washing machine. Easy to use, sleek black stainless steel finish. So quiet you cannot hear it running! Has two main racks and one shallow top rack for utensils. Very happy with purchase. However delivery and install went sideways. The installer didn't have all the parts and informed us we would have to call Costco customer service. It was strange because the unit was not wrapped, in any way, or in a box, just offloaded like it had been removed from someone else's house. It was missing the brackets that hold it to the cabinet and the rubber plugs that go on the inside door frame. It was connected so we could use it but because the mounting brackets were not installed it was sketchy. We did call customer service and although they were happy to rectify the situation, it took a couple of weeks to get the correct one. The next technicians were spot on, knew what they were doing and installed the correct one. But they didn't have a ticket to pick up the incorrect one. So we had to call customer service again and schedule a pick up for later that week. In the meantime, on a different day, a large box truck pulled up into our cul de sac and when I asked them if they were here to pick up the old dishwasher, they said no they had the wrong address. Turns out they were supposed to pick it up so I had to call again. Finally they came and picked if the other unit. The delivery drivers asked us if we wanted a random used chest freezer they had on their truck. We politely declined.

Sentence (English): Ah, a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ "Mostly" Great ] || ---------------- || Ah, a dishwasher. what a droll item to rate. Still, they can be vexing.First, if you use the automatic mode as-is, it does an excellent job of doing its job. Dishes are clean, and well, what more can you ask.Now, if you tinker with this, say, using the app -- look-out. Documentation stinks, choices are a bit limited, and results are less than stellar. I'm sure with multiple tries, I could get the exact results I want -- maybe. Just not worth the time.Two pet peeves which made me drop a star:1) When you run it overnight, and return to it in the morning, the unit is entirely off -- the "Clean" status light included. This is not optimal in a home with more than one person. Did the makers not use this themselves? Why even have that light if it goes out in under an hour -- nobody would "forget" they had just washed the dishes in that amount of time, but in the morning? 2) The lower rack has convenient extra tines that can be dropped down, allowing different ways to load. BUT, this is at the cost of those racks being elevated above the bottom of the main rack. So what? Just try putting a tall glass, or water bottle, there when you have inevitably filled the top rack -- it's going to fall over. I am simply unable to figure out why the elevation was needed -- my previous Bosch accomplished a similar feature without the elevation.

Sentence (English): This is a massive upgrade from the dishwasher we replaced, but it's not perfect.
Comments (English): [ Pricey, but worth it. ] || ---------------- || This is a massive upgrade from the dishwasher we replaced, but it's not perfect. Getting it to connect to my WiFi was a 2 day process (and I still don't know why it finally worked vs all the other times I did the exact same steps). But once you have it connected it's very nice to be notified when a load of dishes is done. This cleans things very nicely, with very few instances of anything being left on a dish or utensil. (And that usually only happens if the mess is REALLY baked on or you've loaded utensils too closely together.) This is still miles better than our old dishwasher, which just seemed to throw food around the inside so that it ended up on everything. The main reason I'm dropping a star on this is that the drying part is really not great. The top/3rd rack (where utensils and plastic stuff typically goes, usually comes out very, very wet, even if you open it up a crack and then forget to unload it for a day. This is fairly typical of all dishwashers, I suppose, especially for plastic items, but I was disappointed since the drying capabilities of this were rated as \"Very Good\" by CR. Oh, and it's VERY quiet. If you hear it making noise it's definitely because you've loaded it wrong.

Sentence (English): Ah, a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ "Mostly" Great ] || ---------------- || Ah, a dishwasher. what a droll item to rate. Still, they can be vexing. First, if you use the automatic mode as-is, it does an excellent job of doing its job. Dishes are clean, and well, what more can you ask. Now, if you tinker with this, say, using the app -- look-out. Documentation stinks, choices are a bit limited, and results are less than stellar. I'm sure with multiple tries, I could get the exact results I want -- maybe. Just not worth the time. Two pet peeves which made me drop a star: 1) When you run it overnight, and return to it in the morning, the unit is entirely off -- the "Clean" status light included. This is not optimal in a home with more than one person. Did the makers not use this themselves? Why even have that light if it goes out in under an hour -- nobody would "forget" they had just washed the dishes in that amount of time, but in the morning? 2) The lower rack has convenient extra tines that can be dropped down, allowing different ways to load. BUT, this is at the cost of those racks being elevated above the bottom of the main rack. So what? Just try putting a tall glass, or water bottle, there when you have inevitably filled the top rack -- it's going to fall over. I am simply unable to figure out why the elevation was needed -- my previous Bosch accomplished a similar feature without the elevation.

Sentence (English): This review is a while coming because I ordered applicances when I started building a new house since they were in short supply and it sat in its box for a few months!
Comments (English): [ Great Dishwasher~ ] || ---------------- || This review is a while coming because I ordered applicances when I started building a new house since they were in short supply and it sat in its box for a few months! I really like this dishwasher in so many ways! stainless steel, inside and out, sleek, no handle, easy open. I especially like that the controls on on the top, where you can see them without leaning over! Very few controls, just choose the soil level (or automatic sensing), push 'start' and shut the door! This machine holds a lot of dishes and cookware. One feature I didn't realize it had was a third top rack designed specifically for utensils and small things so they can fall through the racks! You know when you put that spatula in the top rach and it falls through and stops the spray arm! This rack is genius! The glassware rach has bottle washer spouts! You can turn them on or off depending on whether you have bottles to clean. Simply choose the bottle washer! I actually like the utensil rack. It goes in one place on the bottom rack and is easily removed. The slots in the rack easily take my flatware which has big ends. I like this because it really keeps spoons and forks from nesting so they get clean. Yes, clean. This dishwasher gets things really clean in a couple of hours (epa regs require the longer time to use less water, alas). There is a quick one hour wash, which i have used, but I tend to use the auto sensing and let it go. All of my dishes come out clean AND DRY. Yes! Dry dishes! and sanitized as well! I have challenged this dishwasher with greasy pans, stuck on foods on bakeware and congealed milk in a drinking cup--- all came clean. So, try this dishwasher and I think you will enjoy it. Oh! I forgot to mention that it is very quiet! We watch TV while it's running and it is not noticeable.

I especially like that the controls on on the top, where you can see them without leaning over! Very few controls, just choose the soil level (or automatic sensing), push 'start' and shut the door! You know when you put that spatula in the top rach and it falls through and stops the spray arm! This rack is genius! The glassware rach has bottle washer spouts! I like this because it really keeps spoons and forks from nesting so they get clean. Yes, clean. This dishwasher gets things really clean in a couple of hours (epa regs require the longer time to use less water, alas). There is a quick one hour wash, which i have used, but I tend to use the auto sensing and let it go. All of my dishes come out clean AND DRY. Yes! Dry dishes! and sanitized as well! I have challenged this dishwasher with greasy pans, stuck on foods on bakeware and congealed milk in a drinking cup--- all came clean. So, try this dishwasher and I think you will enjoy it. Oh! I forgot to mention that it is very quiet! We watch TV while it's running and it is not noticeable.

Sentence (English): We bought this dishwasher on a Good Friday sale.
Comments (English): [ Very Happy! ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher on a Good Friday sale. It replaced a 7 yr old Kenmore model that still worked but wouldn't heat water anymore, even after replacing element and thermostat. Even the plastic Rubbermaid leftover containers come out squeaky clean. The third rack is convenient for spatulas, steak knives, etc. The adjustable racks are also helpful. And even though this dishwasher fits into the same space as our old one, the racks in it are actually bigger front to back. I can tell because the side by side rows of dinner plates no longer touch each other. And I should also mention that it runs quietly.

Sentence (English): I've had this about 3 months and am happy with my purchase even if there are some things I don't love.
Comments (English): [ Overall, good - spacing for dishes could be better ] || ---------------- || I've had this about 3 months and am happy with my purchase even if there are some things I don't love. I like the stainless steel tub and love the 3rd rack, we almost never use the silverware basket. The middle rack adjusts very easily and fits surprisingly tall items at the shorter setting, I usually keep it there unless I have some taller cups/water bottles to fit amd even when popping it down there is plenty of room on the bottom for big stuff. Before purchasing I took multiple items that I wanted to make sure fit in our new dishwasher to the home improvement store and put them in all the models I was looking at to see how they fit. My big miss with this one was not taking a regular bowl because ours don't fit on the bottom except along the right side which is the best space for small/medium pans and 9x13 dishes so often not convenient. (To be fair it hit all my other criteria and nothing would ever be absolutely perfect so I would have sucked it up and bought this anyway.) The BEST part of this is I can fit my largest pot and colander beside each other in the back! Plates go sideways in the front then and like to slide around when pulling the rack in and out which is really annoying. (Lost a star for this.) It is only a matter of time before something ends up chipped. The sensor wash consistently left at 1 or 2 dirty dishes on each was so I only use the normal wash. I'm guessing it's because 90% of the dishes would be well cleaned off and it wasn't sensing the others well enough. The energy saving aspect means expect at least 3 hours depending on the cycle you use. The middle rack is shaped with a bit of a dome for the jet arm under it so makes it odd for plastic lids/small plates because they won't stay in the middle and when they end up at the side then you can't use the edge for cups. This combined with the plates moving and bowls not fitting on the bottom lest the second star. It is pretty quiet for the most part. Occasionally it will be a little noisier depending on what is in it.

Comments (English): [ Pricey, but worth it. ] || ---------------- || This is a massive upgrade from the dishwasher we replaced, but it's not perfect. This is fairly typical of all dishwashers, I suppose, especially for plastic items, but I was disappointed since the drying capabilities of this were rated as "Very Good" by CR.Oh, and it's VERY quiet. If you hear it making noise it's definitely because you've loaded it wrong.

Sentence (English): I finally got the dishwasher I've been wanting since moving!
Comments (English): [ A household item worth the money ] || ---------------- || I finally got the dishwasher I've been wanting since moving! Everything from inspection to installation went smoothly! It's so easy to use, you don't even need a manual. Honestly, the dishwasher has nothing but advantages. My kitchen is all about black, but I chose the pink one. It's a beautiful baby pink. I highly recommend it. I especially love how the door opens automatically after the wash cycle is finished. I love it! With my old one, I'd always forget to open it, and if I didn't, the dishes would still be wet. Just like a washing machine, a dishwasher has a tub cleaning function. It depends on how you use it, but you should do it once or twice a month. You can either sprinkle baking soda evenly over the dishwasher and run the wash cycle, or add a tub cleaning detergent. Sentence (English): Toast at 1 year 3 months!
Comments (English): [ Toast at 1 year 3 months ] || ---------------- || Toast at 1 year 3 months! We are a family of 4 who try to eat at home as often as possible, we run our dishwasher 1x a day (which is assumed pretty typical for a family of 4). From day one the dishwasher had to be run on the heavy setting with the steam option and the high temp option on in order for the dishes to come out even remotely clean. Even with these on there was always a dish or 3 that needed to be rewatched. After a visit from an LG service technician in the beginning due to not being happy with performance we were told us to only use Finish brand detergent (previously using cascade) and after making the switch we were down to only 1 dish each wash in need of rewashing. Mind you there is no dried on food on our dishes, we do a quick pass under the faucet and then the dishwasher is ran everyday. Also important to note is that even with the extra dry option on, the dishes come out so wet they need to air dry overnight (min of 5-6 hours, sometimes more like 8-10 hours and we do not use a humidifier in our house) on drying mats on our counter before they can be put away without causing water damage to our cabinets or they have to be hand dried which we unfortunately do not have time to dedicate to doing every day. Fast forward to the 1 year mark and the dishwasher started making a very loud what we would call helicopter noise, shortly after the noise started many dishes started coming out of the wash completely dirty. LG phone support concluded possibly the motor bearings or motor and even though these should be covered under the 10 year warranty they could not guarantee that was the issue and we would be responsible for the bill if it was something else. So LG suggested using our purchased store warranty to play it safe. Warranty company from the purchasing store (we bought extra 5 year warranty thankfully) sent repair company that first replaced a spray arm, then replaced an actuator on another visit and on visit 3 suggested replacement of the entire unit (thankfully) under the warranty. Unfortunately the multiple repairs and waiting for parts (no fault of repair company, they were great) had us without a functioning dishwasher for almost 3 months from the time it started to have issues until replacement was recommended. If you are like our family and depend on a functioning dishwasher daily you might want to avoid an LG dishwasher, just our opinion based off our experience. Not sure if ours was a lemon or if this is typical for this model but regardless we wanted to share in case anything we learned or experienced could help others. We are hoping to return to a Bosch after this (still in process of waiting to hear back from warranty company through the store) our last one made it 8 years before the door literally fell off, and after reattaching it by carefully rigging it with string it still continued to put out a clean load each time we ran it until it was pulled out for this LG to go in.

Sentence (English): I've had this dishwasher for a month now and am pretty pleased with it.
Comments (English): [ 300 Series Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I've had this dishwasher for a month now and am pretty pleased with it. I originally had some concerns that the Bosch method of drying dishes wouldn't work as well as models with a heating elemet but I worried over noting - the drying process works perfectly - just don't rush the drying time. Regarding other things: the third rack for silverware works out very nicely; the middle and lower racks work well for everyting but bowl shaped things - it seems like bowls want to tip over because the support prongs are located where they don't quite support bowls. One other thing is that you need WiFi to tell if the washer is done - the end of cycle lights turn off a few minutes after the cycle completes so you either need to check the dishes or check WiFi. The control panel is nicely laid out and easy to understand. The dishwasher is also nice and quiet. Overall, a very nice product.

You can also set the unit for sanitizing and extra time for the drying cycle.

Sentence (English): It had the first AAA+ stainless steel integrated dishwasher model that BOSCH launched on the market.
Comments (English): [ Super recommended: my 2nd BOSH dishwasher ] || ---------------- || It had the first AAA+ stainless steel integrated dishwasher model that BOSCH launched on the market. Purchased in 2002 for €1,200. Large family with intensive daily use of two dishwashers a day for almost 22 years. A true champion that was still working. I was looking to change the baskets that were deteriorated from so much use and it was incredible that BOSH after so many years has all the spare parts, even the smallest screw on my old dishwasher. It has been difficult for me to get rid of the old one because of all my appliances it was by far the best and they are all high-end from top brands. I had no doubt that I would buy another BOSH again for quality, efficiency, technology, easy and intuitive handling and, above all, for its fantastic technical service and if any part deteriorates over time, I will have no problem being able to replace it. If with the old one without any breakdown in 22 years, I was satisfied with the new one even more. To highlight the cutlery tray, it is fantastic. Before with the basket I lacked space and now I have plenty of space. As for programs, it has 3 more than the previous one: machine cleaning, ECO, Silence 50. Also 3 more functionalities than the previous one that are wonderful: automatic door opening, half load and SpeedPerfect+. If the old one was silent, this model is super silent, it even makes you doubt if it is working because there are washing sections where you cannot hear absolutely anything. Finally, the Home Connect app, being able to configure the functions and program from your mobile is simple and adapts to current times. I have been using it for 3 weeks and my dishes have been rejuvenated. Drying and shine a 10. In short, IT ONLY NEEDS TO TALK.

Sentence (English): I bought this because I didn't like seeing my mother-in-law and father-in-law standing and hurting their backs while doing the dishes at my in-laws' house.
Comments (English): I bought this because I didn't like seeing my mother-in-law and father-in-law standing and hurting their backs while doing the dishes at my in-laws' house. It also served as a year-end gift. They are very satisfied. Since they don't use a water purifier, there were no holes in the countertop, so I ran the cord through the cabinet underneath to avoid making any holes. Older people tend to think the cost of drilling holes is a waste, haha. It was the first time I saw a method where they swapped the boiling water cord for an extension cord, ran it long, and routed it inside the pot cabinet; it didn't really detract from the interior. Sentence (English): So far, I like it.
Comments (English): [ So far, so good. ] || ---------------- || So far, I like it. It runs for half of the time of my previous Maytag (that on the “heavy duty” mode would run for four hours and 13 minutes), and gets the dishes just as clean. It's very quiet, so much so that I often am unaware that it's running. I like the third rack a lot more than I thought I was going to, and wondered how I ever managed to do without it. There's a reason for that third rack, however, as the utensil holder, with only three sections, is so small as to nearly be useless. The overflow from that utensil holder is what finds its way to the third rack. On the plus side, having a small utensil holder means there is more space on the bottom rack. When I find a bit perplexing about this model is the strange configuration of the prongs on the bottom rack. Dishes need to be put in at rather strange angles, and I find that, unlike with my previous dishwasher, I can't manage to put in large racks and cookie sheets. It is allegedly operational through an app. I was never able to get the app to work properly or connect the dishwasher, so that aspect doesn't work. On the plus side, I doubt that I would've used that anyway The true test will be how long this lasts. My previous dishwasher had trouble from the get go, and only made it seven years.

Sentence (English): First of all, this dishwasher is 1/4" narrower than American brands, and in tight spaces, this makes all the difference.
Comments (English): [ Slim, large, and quiet ] || ---------------- || First of all, this dishwasher is 1/4" narrower than American brands, and in tight spaces, this makes all the difference. Second, I like the third rack up top to for silverware and cooking utensils. In additional to being handy, it leaves beaucoup room on the bottom rack for dishes, etc. Third, it is quiet. Really, really quiet. Fourth, it gets dishes very clean and dry (except for some plastic lids and the bottoms of some mugs, but only some). It has multiple adjustments (watch the videos; they're short and very clear).
